capabilities.justification: The fuzz executor runs every target execution in a freshly spawned domain (Domain.spawn, VER06r 4) so the engine regains control at its deadline; the test suites also spawn domains to prove that concurrent charges to one budget tree are atomic, that a spawned domain inherits the ambient scope, that a retained handle is inert in another domain, and that a domain outliving its scope holds a spent handle.

The fuzz executor reads the wall clock (Unix.gettimeofday; the unix library ships with the OCaml compiler) to bound its wait for a worker domain (VER06r 4). Only an elapsed-time deadline is computed: no calendar time, timezone or date is used.
The fuzz executor waits for its worker domain with Unix.sleepf, backing off from 50 microseconds to 1 ms, instead of spinning (VER06r 4); the tests use it to build honest slow targets.

justification: In-memory property and fuzz engines. The libraries have no filesystem, network, process, or environment access (the CI flag is a parameter); tests embed the pbt-v1 and fuzz-v1 corpora and the Go reference-vector table as OCaml strings. The only capabilities are in-process domains and the wall clock and short sleeps that bound a wait.
